question: Is historical passive -li independently productive as internal morphology before outer derivational suffixes, or is tsane-li-ameke an isolated architecture?

secondary_comparable_forms_not_promoted.reason: Merrill cites it as a comparison to tsanelíameke but the audited passage does not provide a full independent morpheme-by-morpheme derivation.

epistemic_limits: Examples in -li-la demonstrate historical -li as internal morphology before an outer suffix; they do not constitute additional li-ameke tokens.
Do not segment tschutschelíameke automatically until an explicit analysis or sufficient independent paradigm is found.
Do not infer a universal historical rule -li-ameke > modern -li-ame from morphotactic compatibility alone.
next_tests: Audit tschutschá / tschutschelíla / tschutschelíameke as a possible second historical li-ameke family.
Search all historical *líameke strings and classify them by independent root/paradigm evidence.
Compare the historical li-outer-suffix architecture to modern explicitly segmented li-ame across varieties without transferring function automatically.
